# Paper and audit scope

*You give them something to eat: Dietary Diversity, Coverage, and Catholic Aid in Rwanda*. Second genuine referee revision, preparing third submission. Public branch codex/research. Internal self-audit follows the retained public JPE TEMPLATE.qmd criteria/MIT attribution. No journal manuscript ID, official JPE certification or independent full replication is asserted.

# Data, rights and sources

All default inputs are supplied. Corrected Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15881329 is open CC BY 4.0; actual metadata/correction/checksum are in docs/sources/zenodo-rights.json. Withdrawn/restricted predecessor excluded. Household panel: 5,506 rows/52 numeric fields; supplementary household panel: 5,506 matching rows; child panel: 7,356 numeric rows. Arbitrary linkage keys replace source identifiers; contacts, exact geography/dates, free text and administrative lists are excluded. Field review supplements numeric checks without guaranteeing universal anonymity.

Both source extractors verify archive MD5/SHA256, exact source members and independently pinned output bytes. Altered data plus rewritten generated provenance and a corrupt source archive are rejected. Original source ZIP is ignored. Source-to-extract replication starts from corrected processed panels, not all upstream questionnaire cleaning. Codebooks distinguish inherited economic/anthropometric preprocessing, food recall/transforms and unrecovered monetary price base.

Item information identifies 1,730 endline diets; 1,728 complete modules are the initial sample. All 1,793 baseline eligibles receive interval endpoints. The one-household discrepancy from the original 1,794 is retained. Twenty smaller public CSV views reconstruct three immutable inputs byte for byte; they are aliases for inspection, not extra observations or evidence of independent execution.

# Software and execution

Python 3.12.10, NumPy 2.5.2, pandas 3.0.5, SciPy 1.18.1, Matplotlib 3.11.1; exact tested direct/transitive packages in requirements-lock.txt. Existing MiKTeX 25.12 supplies optional pdflatex. Optional extraction openpyxl 3.1.5; visual/cold-copy tools PyMuPDF/Pillow; initial independent Stata/MP 19 reference uses built-in commands. Requested optional LR prose screen is separate. No language model processes data or enters scientific estimates.

Windows 11 x64, eight available logical processors; no GPU/API/network after installation. Allow 2 GB RAM/150 MB reproduction space plus packages; physical RAM not measured. Current master/PDF runtime 56.40 seconds. Single command `python run.py --pdf`; omit --pdf for all numerical outputs; --from-source runs direct-ZIP reconstruction.

Master checks references, estimates initial ANCOVA, constructs conditional ratio/finite regions, solves diversified allocation and cost scenarios, accounts for child cohorts, computes ANCOVA CR2/omissions, records failed block stress tests, builds exhibits, runs three validators and compiles three times. Scientific paths are project relative. Initial 9,999 village multipliers and revised 99,999 block multipliers use seed 20260930; synthetic stress uses seed 20261001, 800 assignments/scenario and 4,999 diagnostic multipliers.

# Exhibits and inferential scope

Output map derives actual manuscript numbering: 24 cited tables, 1 cited figure, three generated macro sets. Total generated output is 26 tables/five figures; unused supplementary plots/tables are labeled uncited. Numerical sources and builder lines are provided. Source facts, mathematical claims and citations need review beyond successful execution.

Initial families: 204 primary, 96 economic, 80 food, ten heterogeneity, five observation. Revised exploratory block families: 184 GK/cash, 828 pairwise and 1,656 endpoints after affine deduplication. Separate finite families: 276 full-baseline primitive arm/endpoints and 138 observed primitives. Child baseline-cohort, endline-due and ineligible estimates each have separate fifteen-test Holm families. Separate events do not create one paper-wide 95% guarantee. All extensions retain exploratory amendment history.

# Actual verification

Core 33/33 with optional independent Stata output (32/32 in cold copy without it); revision 92/92; decision 14/14. Initial five ANCOVA coefficients/SEs agree with Stata within 1.3e-13/5.2e-15. Coherent CDF identities, independent vertex/adversary LPs, ratio inversion fixtures, bounded-sampling exponential comparisons, weight scaling, zero denominators, child partition and provenance checks pass. CR2 working-model expectation identities pass. These are implementation checks, not a validation of the failed multiplier approximation.

Synthetic 22-block joint coverage is 695/800 with equal weights and 592/800 with unequal weights for fifteen mean comparisons. The sparse-effect scenario covers 800/800 after full-support guards. Failures remain in blocked-validation.json; the master prints them and does not pretend they are passed nominal-coverage tests. The finite conditional bound is derived separately under exchangeable quota assignment/independent blocks/fixed weights and stable potential outcomes. Full-frame sampling representativeness is not proved.

Current cold-output comparison: 80/80, including 31-page PDF text. Separate-environment published-source check for this third submission remains pending. The existing fresh-environment JSON records the earlier scientific commit 63987ae and its 32-page PDF; it must not be interpreted as checking the current source. Runtime metadata, PDF timestamps and optional Stata reference are excluded from byte comparisons. Historical first-submission fresh-install and second-submission 60-comparison audits remain recoverable in Git.

All 31 rendered pages/contact sheets were inspected; main decision tables, figure, title and proofs checked at higher resolution. Current log has no overfull boxes or unresolved references. Compilation and visual review are distinct checks.

# Limits and classification

HDDS is household food access rather than child nutrition. The finite allocation bound is conditional, wide, and not an impossibility theorem. Smaller block-region losses are explicitly exploratory. Transport needs comparable weighting, original delivery, stable proportional costs and no changed cross-village interference. Cash overhead was standardized to a separate national program of 56,127 beneficiary households for each transfer amount. Mixed-program marginal/activation costs and hard realized budgets are not observed. Cost/take-up scenarios hold effects fixed. Saving theory is illustrative and not identified mediation.
